c.tagline: Riverside Miao and Tujia old town of stilt houses, covered bridges, and lantern-lit nights on the Tuo River.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but are limited since the pedestrianized old town is car-free; most visitors use the Didi ride-hailing app or walk.

emergency.note: 119 is for fire; English-speaking operators are not guaranteed, so hotel staff assistance is recommended.

avoid.reason: Watch for tourist overcharging, pushy boat-ride and photo touts, and crushing crowds along the Tuojiang riverfront on holidays.

hood_desc: The scenic heart of Fenghuang along the Tuo River, lined with stilted wooden houses (diaojiaolou), riverside bars, and boat docks; the liveliest and most photographed area, especially at night.
A quieter residential quarter around the historic East Gate Tower and old city wall; good for travelers wanting easy access to the sights without the nightlife crowds.
lodging: Fenghuang Old Town International Youth Hostel

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as is standard in China.

transit.hours: Local buses run roughly 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM; the old town itself is pedestrianized and explored on foot.
transit.pay: Cash or mobile payment (Alipay/WeChat Pay) on board; no rechargeable transit card for casual visitors.
transit.note: The ancient town core is pedestrianized and car-free; buses and taxis are used mainly to reach the long-distance bus station or nearby attractions like Qiliang Cave.

train: Jishou East railway station (high-speed rail, ~1 hr away)
bus: Fenghuang long-distance bus station (coaches to Jishou, Zhangjiajie, Changsha)

car.idp: Not valid; Chinese driving license required

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to Fenghuang (~45 min, several times daily)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected or customary in China, including in Fenghuang; a small tip for a very helpful private guide is fine but never required.

food.name: Miao sour fish soup (suantang yu)
food.desc: Tuojiang river fish simmered in a scarlet broth of fermented tomato and chilli, served bubbling in a clay pot. The signature Miao dish of western Hunan.

places.name: Laogen Restaurant
places.note: Long-running local favourite widely named in recent guides for its clay-pot sour fish soup.

places.name: Restaurants on Hongqiao Middle Road
places.note: The strip a block back from the water; same dish, noticeably better prices than riverfront tables.

places.name: Riverside eateries along Tuojiang
places.note: Stilt-house terraces over the river; pay a premium for the view, so check prices before sitting.

food.name: Blood duck (xueba ya)
food.desc: Duck stir-fried hard with chilli and ginger, then bound with cakes of glutinous rice set in duck blood. Rich, smoky and genuinely local to Fenghuang.

places.name: Junzi Restaurant
places.note: Regularly recommended for blood duck at modest per-head prices; order it with rice.

places.name: Hongqiao Middle Road family restaurants
places.note: Neighbourhood kitchens where locals eat; blood duck is usually on the wall menu.

food.name: Rice tofu (mi doufu)
food.desc: Soft pale blocks set from rice milk, cut into cubes and dressed cold with chilli oil, vinegar, garlic and pickles. The town's everyday cheap snack.

places.name: Snack stalls on Huilongge Street
places.note: Rows of small stands ladling rice tofu into bowls to order for a few yuan.

places.name: East Gate snack street
places.note: Busy evening food lane just inside the old city wall; good for grazing several snacks.

food.name: Ginger candy (jiangtang)
food.desc: Fresh ginger boiled with sugar, then pulled by hand on a wooden hook until pale and pliable. Sweet first, hot after, and made in the shop window.

places.name: Zhang family ginger candy shops
places.note: The best-known local name; watch the pulling demonstration and taste before you buy.

places.name: Candy shops along Huilongge Street
places.note: Dozens of shops in a row, nearly all offering free samples; compare before committing.

food.name: Sour radish and Miao pickles
food.desc: Crunchy radish and long beans soured in earthenware jars, sold on a stick or by the bowl. Miao households pickle almost everything for the wet months.

places.name: East Gate snack street
places.note: Stalls sell sour radish on sticks for pocket change; a good chilli-cutting palate reset.

places.name: Fenghuang morning market
places.area: New town, north of the river
places.note: Where locals buy pickles by weight from the jar, well away from the tourist lanes.

food.name: Fenghuang shrimp cakes and rice noodles
food.desc: River shrimp pressed into batter and deep fried into crisp discs, often eaten with a breakfast bowl of soupy Xiangxi rice noodles.

places.name: Noodle shops near the North Gate
places.note: Open early for the local breakfast crowd; shrimp cakes fried fresh at the door.

places.name: Riverside snack stalls along Tuojiang
places.note: Cakes fried to order through the day; eat them hot or they turn heavy.

food.name: Miao rice wine (mijiu)
food.desc: Cloudy, lightly sweet wine fermented from glutinous rice, poured from jars at village feasts and sold by the bottle in the old town.

places.name: Rice wine shops on Huilongge Street
places.note: Wooden barrels out front with tasting cups; strengths vary a lot, so sample first.

places.name: Riverside restaurants along Tuojiang
places.note: Serve house rice wine by the jug alongside sour fish soup, the traditional pairing.

food.name: Guzhang maojian green tea
food.desc: Downy spring green tea from the hills of Xiangxi just north of town, brewed light and grassy. The regional tea of choice with a heavy, spicy meal.

places.name: Tea houses along Huilongge Street
places.note: Quiet upstairs rooms above the shopping lane; sold loose by weight as well as by the pot.

places.name: Teahouse terraces above Tuojiang
places.note: Balcony seating over the water and the stepping stones; best in the late afternoon.

landmarks: Fenghuang Ancient Town
A riverside labyrinth of Ming- and Qing-era streets, city gates and lantern-lit alleys widely hailed as China's most beautiful ancient town.
Diaojiaolou Stilt Houses on the Tuojiang
Rows of centuries-old wooden houses propped on spindly stilts above the river, their reflections doubling the magic at dawn and dusk.
Hong Bridge (Hongqiao)
A grand Ming-dynasty covered bridge-tower spanning the Tuojiang, its galleried upper floor offering the classic postcard view of the old town.
Tuojiang River Boat Ride
A gentle wooden-sampan glide beneath stilt houses and stepping-stone crossings, with boatmen singing folk songs against a backdrop of misty hills.
North Gate Tower (Bei Men)
The best preserved of Fenghuang's ancient city gates, a stout stone-and-timber tower guarding the famous stepping stones across the river.
Former Residence of Shen Congwen
The tranquil courtyard birthplace of one of modern China's greatest writers, whose lyrical books made his hometown Fenghuang famous.
Wanming Pagoda
A slender riverside pagoda rising above the lower Tuojiang, glowing gold at night as one of the town's most photographed silhouettes.
Longevity Palace (Wanshou Gong)
A handsome Qing-era guild-hall complex of carved halls and courtyards, now housing the Fenghuang folk art and history exhibitions.
Yang Family Ancestral Hall
An exquisitely carved 19th-century ancestral temple of a prominent military clan, tucked into the old town's northern lanes.
Southern Great Wall (Miaojiang Great Wall)
The restored Ming-dynasty frontier wall snaking over hills outside town, built to control the Miao borderlands and walkable for sweeping views.

train.note: Fenghuang has no international trains. Fenghuang Ancient City Station opened on the Zhangjiajie-Jishou-Huaihua high-speed line and is well outside the town, linked to the old streets by a maglev shuttle and express buses; Changsha is about 2-2.5 hours away and Zhangjiajie 50-65 minutes. Book on 12306 with your passport, and budget 30-40 minutes for the transfer at each end. Trains are far quicker than the old bus route from Jishou, which is what most visitors used before the line opened.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Fenghuang. Buses from Jishou North station leave every 30 minutes (¥20, 30-60 minutes) and are the cheapest approach; there are also eight daily coaches from Changsha (¥120, about 8 hours), hourly services from Huaihua to the Western Station (¥40, 1.5 hours), around four a day from Zhangjiajie (¥65-75, 4.5-5.5 hours) and one daily from Guilin South at 11:00 (¥160, about 6 hours). Tickets are bought at the terminal counters on the day.

ferry.note: Fenghuang has no passenger ferry services - it is far inland on the shallow Tuo River. The wooden sampans poled along the river through the old town are short sightseeing rides sold from the riverbank, not transport to anywhere.

half.name: Furong (Hibiscus) Ancient Town
half.blurb: Stilt-house village built into a waterfall on the Youshui River, less commercialized and quieter than Fenghuang itself.

half.name: Dehang Canyon & Miao Village
half.blurb: Karst canyon with a suspended glass walkway and a traditional Miao settlement offering a contrast to Fenghuang's crowds.

full.name: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
full.blurb: Towering sandstone pillars that inspired the floating mountains of Avatar, reached by cable car and glass walkways.
